newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies off sharply on cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies off sharply on cash ideas.

text.p: Expectations of further weakness in cash pork prices and hog markets early next week weighed on CME hog and pork belly futures late but short covering pared losses in hogs at the close, traders said.
Hog futures ended off 0.950 cent per lb to up 0.025 with February off 0.700 at 74.900 cents and April off most at 74.750. Pork bellies finished off 2.575 to 1.325 with February off 1.575 at 77.850.

A weak technical picture added to pressure from declining cash pork prices and expected light packer demand for hogs next week to press hog futures. Cash hog prices should be lower on Monday, traders said.

Moderating weather should allow an increased flow of hogs to market at the same time packers will be trying to recoup some of their margins that were lost when cold weather cut hog marketings. Packer margins are basically $3 per cwt in the red, some sources said.

Technically, futures look weaker as February neared its 40-day average and fell to its lowest level since October 31. April slipped to its lowest level since late December on the break, chartists said.
However, short covering pared losses in the final minutes.

In hog options, LIT division of First Options notably sold February 75 puts and bought April 72 calls early while commercials did risk reversals in July and August, buying July 72 puts and selling 86 calls and buying August 72 puts and selling 82 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures fell on the weak tone to cash product and eased to one-week lows. Cash bellies have lost as much as $5 per cwt in the past couple of days and demand remained light despite less-than-expected hog slaughter the past couple of weeks. Losses were pared in February at the close, sources noted.

ABN Chicogo Corp was a light buyer early but general local and commission house pressure turned price down into sell stops around midsession. Continued rolling out of short positions in February into March limited the loss in February, pit sources said.
